1	# Authentication and environment
2	
3	Use the configured Quest Platform service target. The default is production;
4	stage is selected only when `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage` is explicitly configured for
5	a controlled stage run. The publisher project can be a test or live project.
6	Never change the service target or credential source as a fallback after an
7	error.
8	
9	Service credentials and certificate configuration belong to the configured
10	integration. Do not hardcode private hostnames, private CA details or service
11	keys in this public skill. For Quest Platform publisher routes, use the
12	versioned [API contract](qp-api-contract.md), then make a read-only request
13	against the public gateway selected by `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` before any write.
14	Production OpenAPI is intentionally unavailable. Consult stage OpenAPI only
15	when `XSOLLA_QP_ENV=stage`. On a production run, never fetch stage OpenAPI or
16	any non-selected target; stage OpenAPI does not prove production behavior.
17	
18	## Services
19	
20	The integration may expose separate services for quest configuration, event
21	ingestion, execution read-back and Web3 catalog lookups. Use only the service
22	that owns the requested operation. For Quest Platform configuration, event
23	ingestion and execution read-back, use the versioned route contract above.
24	Consult published OpenAPI only when the selected target exposes it. A missing
25	route is not replaced with a guessed path or a route from another target.
26	
27	## Minting service
28	
29	Use the production Web3 minting service for read-only catalog validation at
30	`https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-prod.srv.local`. Its `GET /skus`
31	and `GET /metadata/sku/{sku}` routes are public read operations and do not use
32	the Quest Platform project API key. Never call a claim endpoint directly.
33	Rewards are issued only by an activated quest.
34	
35	For candidate discovery, page through `GET /skus?project={project}&limit=100&offset={offset}`
36	using the already-resolved publisher project as the lookup scope, then match
37	the requested name against the returned item names. This project value scopes
38	the read only; do not use it as the reward's catalog project unless the minting
39	service returns it as `projectId`. Require HTTP 200 and a valid JSON object
40	with a `projectId` string, numeric `count`, and `items` array on every page.
41	Abort the lookup on any HTTP error, malformed response, or project mismatch;
42	never treat an error as an empty page. Continue with offsets 0, 100, 200, and
43	so on until a valid page contains no items. The optional `search` parameter
44	reports `searchScope: "this page only"` and is not an exhaustive catalog
45	search, so do not use it to prove uniqueness or absence. The response's
46	`projectId` is the catalog project to carry forward. Validate each plausible
47	candidate with `GET /metadata/sku/{sku}?project={projectId}`; require HTTP 200
48	and a JSON `name` matching the catalog name. Abort on any failed or malformed
49	metadata read. Read the complete catalog before deciding that a name has zero
50	or one matches. Do not issue writes to this service.
51	
52	The stage host is
53	`https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local` and may be used
54	only when the explicit [stage demo gate](stage-demo.md#gate) passes. A
55	production run never falls back to stage, or vice versa.
56	
57	For a named item, resolve it through the minting catalog reads above. Preserve
58	the `projectId` returned with the verified item and validate that exact
59	`(catalog_project, sku)` pair in the metadata read before using it in the
60	`web3_item` body. A zero or ambiguous result stops the flow.
61	
62	## Credential
63	
64	Use the selected merchant and project settings supplied by the configured
65	integration. Never ask the publisher to paste a secret into chat or print a
66	header.
67	
68	The shared project-local configuration uses these names. A process environment
69	may provide the same values instead:
70	
71	| Value | Use |
72	|---|---|
73	| `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` | merchant scope for the project |
74	| `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` | Quest Platform project scope |
75	| `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY` | project API key |
76	
77	Never print, log or commit credentials or encoded headers. For Quest Platform
78	publisher routes, the API contract requires HTTP Basic with the configured
79	merchant ID as the username and the project API key as the password. Do not
80	generalize this QP-specific Basic format to Catalog, Store or unrelated APIs.
81	Do not send multiple auth schemes in one request.
82	
83	Read `.env` only as text; never source, execute, echo or interpolate the file.
84	Never open `.env` in a file viewer or print it, and never paste a credential
85	value into command text, a script file, a log or a reply. Parse the values
86	inside the same command that sends the request, so they reach the HTTP client
87	without ever appearing in the command line or its output. One safe pattern
88	feeds the Basic pair to curl through its config on standard input:
89	
90	```sh
91	python3 -c 'import pathlib; e=dict(l.split("=",1) for l in pathlib.Path(".env").read_text().splitlines() if "=" in l and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")); print("user = \"%s:%s\"" % (e["XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID"].strip(), e["XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY"].strip()))' | curl -sS -K - "<route>"
92	```
93	
94	Resolve the three credential names as an all-or-nothing set:
95	
96	1. If all three process-environment values are present and non-empty, use that
97	   complete set.
98	2. Otherwise, if all three project-local `.env` values are present and
99	   non-empty, use that complete set.
100	3. Never combine process values with `.env` values. If neither source is
101	   complete, stop before network calls and tell the publisher to set
102	   `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID`, `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID`, and
103	   `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY` in the project-local `.env` or process environment.
104	
105	For the Quest service selector, a process-environment value takes precedence
106	when present; otherwise read `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` from project-local `.env`. If the
107	selector is absent from both places, use `production`. Only `production` and
108	explicit `stage` are accepted. An explicitly present empty, whitespace-only, or
109	unsupported value is an error: stop before network calls and ask the publisher
110	to set it to `production` or `stage`. `XSOLLA_QP_ENV` selects Quest Platform
111	services (configuration, event ingestion, and execution read-back). It does not
112	select the Web3 catalog or minting lane, which remains production as documented
113	in Minting service. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:** the one exception is the
114	[stage demo gate](stage-demo.md#gate), which uses stage catalog and mint reads
115	for the demo scope. It is not a credential and merchant setup must preserve it.
116	Do not infer a target by probing hosts or by trying a credential against
117	multiple gateways.
118	
119	The versioned API contract maps `production` to
120	`https://quests-platform.xsolla.com` and `stage` to
121	`https://quests-stage.xsolla.com`.
122	
123	The catalog project is not a credential and must come from the resolved item,
124	never from the Quest Platform project by default.
125	
126	## The merchant id in the path
127	
128	When the contract uses merchant and project path parameters, both must come
129	from the same resolved credential set. Never take them from
130	the quest body, a read-back row, an earlier answer or a guess. A developer who
131	names another merchant or project needs the matching credential set.
132	
133	The server may stamp publisher and project fields from the route. Read them
134	back after creation and stop if they do not match the resolved scope.
135	
136	## Project-scoped routes
137	
138	Use the merchant/project-scoped Quest Platform route family in the
139	[versioned API contract](qp-api-contract.md):
140	
141	| Operation | Use |
142	|---|---|
143	| `GET /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}` | verify scope and visibility |
144	| `GET /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}/quests` | find an existing quest by paging |
145	| `POST /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}/quests` | create with `status: inactive` for a draft |
146	| `GET` or `PUT /api/v2/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}/quests/{quest_id}` | read or replace one quest |
147	
148	Do not substitute an account-scoped, publisher-scoped or unscoped route from a
149	different authentication lane. A route absent from the versioned contract is
150	not called.
151	
152	## When a route is missing
153	
154	A 404 router miss means the method and path are not deployed at that location.
155	It is not proof of a bad credential or missing project:
156	
157	1. Stop and do not retry a guessed route.
158	2. For Quest Platform routes (configuration, event ingestion, execution
159	   read-back), compare with the versioned API contract. Consult published
160	   OpenAPI only when the selected target exposes it.
161	3. If the contract documents the same operation under another route, show the
162	   developer the proposed route and ask before calling it. For a write, show
163	   the request again.
164	4. If the operation is absent or not publisher-usable, report that it is
165	   unavailable and stop.
166	
167	## Reading a 401 or 404
168	
169	Report the service's response body verbatim when it explains the blocker, but
170	do not expose credential material. Keep these distinctions:
171	
172	- authentication required or invalid credentials means the selected
173	  credential was not accepted;
174	- a project-not-found response is not enough to distinguish an unknown,
175	  un-onboarded or differently scoped project;
176	- a plain router-miss response means the route is wrong or unavailable;
177	- a missing quest response means it is not found or not visible with this
178	  credential.
179	
180	Do not switch to another credential, environment or route after a failure.
181	
182	## Onboarding
183	
184	If the selected service contract documents onboarding, treat it as a separate
185	write. Offer it only after the developer confirms that the selected project
186	belongs to the selected merchant and provides any required non-secret names.
187	Show the request without credentials and wait for explicit confirmation.
188	
189	After a timeout or server error, read the project before offering onboarding
190	again. Never use onboarding as a probe and never infer that a 404 requires it.
191	
192	## Service preflight
193	
194	Run one read-only preflight per service, only when the task needs that service:
195	
196	- Quest configuration: read the selected project and the quest list.
197	- Event ingestion: confirm the event route and publisher Basic lane from
198	  [`qp-api-contract.md`](qp-api-contract.md) (including its production probe)
199	  before sending anything. If the contract marks the route unavailable to the
200	  publisher key, stop and report it; do not guess a host or fetch OpenAPI on
201	  production.
202	- Execution read-back: confirm the read-back route, auth lane and probe from
203	  [`qp-api-contract.md`](qp-api-contract.md) before any query. If the publisher
204	  Basic lane is not accepted, or the production probe is a router miss, stop
205	  and report that read-back is unavailable; never use an internal key.
206	- Web3 catalog: resolve the named item and validate its catalog project and
207	  SKU; for a Web3 reward, when a recipient is known, also check the recipient
208	  wallet during the read-only work before the proposal, or otherwise before any
209	  publication write, and again before the event.
210	
211	Bring-up and preflight are GET-only. Ask before any other call.
212	
213	## Scope
214	
215	Read the selected project and show only a short name/status summary
216	in the normal publisher reply. Before the first write, confirm that it is the
217	intended project. On create, verify the returned publisher and project fields.
218	On a full `PUT`, preserve the values from the latest single-quest read.
219	
220	Never guess a scope or silently switch projects, merchants or credentials.
221	
222	## Service key: staff only
223	
224	Internal service or master keys are outside this public skill. Never request,
225	print or use one as a fallback for a publisher credential. If the
226	developer asks for an internal lane, stop and direct them to the Quest
227	Platform owner.
228	
229	## Route families this skill does not drive
230	
231	Do not probe account administration, workspace administration, credential
232	management, grant administration or data-republish routes. They are outside
233	quest setup and require a separately documented owner-approved integration.
234	
235	## Deployment status
236	
237	A project read does not prove that event submission, execution read-back or
238	Web3 payout is ready. Confirm each required operation against the contract for
239	its selected service target before using it. Never switch targets as a
240	fallback.

1. Stop and do not retry a guessed route.
2. For Quest Platform routes (configuration, event ingestion, execution
   read-back), compare with the versioned API contract. Consult published
   OpenAPI only when the selected target exposes it.
3. If the contract documents the same operation under another route, show the
   developer the proposed route and ask before calling it. For a write, show
   the request again.
4. If the operation is absent or not publisher-usable, report that it is
   unavailable and stop.

## Reading a 401 or 404

Report the service's response body verbatim when it explains the blocker, but
do not expose credential material. Keep these distinctions:

- authentication required or invalid credentials means the selected
  credential was not accepted;
- a project-not-found response is not enough to distinguish an unknown,
  un-onboarded or differently scoped project;
- a plain router-miss response means the route is wrong or unavailable;
- a missing quest response means it is not found or not visible with this
  credential.

Do not switch to another credential, environment or route after a failure.

## Onboarding

If the selected service contract documents onboarding, treat it as a separate
write. Offer it only after the developer confirms that the selected project
belongs to the selected merchant and provides any required non-secret names.
Show the request without credentials and wait for explicit confirmation.

After a timeout or server error, read the project before offering onboarding
again. Never use onboarding as a probe and never infer that a 404 requires it.

## Service preflight

Run one read-only preflight per service, only when the task needs that service:

- Quest configuration: read the selected project and the quest list.
- Event ingestion: confirm the event route and publisher Basic lane from
  [`qp-api-contract.md`](qp-api-contract.md) (including its production probe)
  before sending anything. If the contract marks the route unavailable to the
  publisher key, stop and report it; do not guess a host or fetch OpenAPI on
  production.
- Execution read-back: confirm the read-back route, auth lane and probe from
  [`qp-api-contract.md`](qp-api-contract.md) before any query. If the publisher
  Basic lane is not accepted, or the production probe is a router miss, stop
  and report that read-back is unavailable; never use an internal key.
- Web3 catalog: resolve the named item and validate its catalog project and
  SKU; for a Web3 reward, when a recipient is known, also check the recipient
  wallet during the read-only work before the proposal, or otherwise before any
  publication write, and again before the event.

Bring-up and preflight are GET-only. Ask before any other call.

## Scope

Read the selected project and show only a short name/status summary
in the normal publisher reply. Before the first write, confirm that it is the
intended project. On create, verify the returned publisher and project fields.
On a full `PUT`, preserve the values from the latest single-quest read.

Never guess a scope or silently switch projects, merchants or credentials.

## Service key: staff only

Internal service or master keys are outside this public skill. Never request,
print or use one as a fallback for a publisher credential. If the
developer asks for an internal lane, stop and direct them to the Quest
Platform owner.

## Route families this skill does not drive

Do not probe account administration, workspace administration, credential
management, grant administration or data-republish routes. They are outside
quest setup and require a separately documented owner-approved integration.

## Deployment status

A project read does not prove that event submission, execution read-back or
Web3 payout is ready. Confirm each required operation against the contract for
its selected service target before using it. Never switch targets as a
fallback.

content.content:
1	# Web3 rewards
2	
3	This skill supports the production Web3 reward path only. A named item always
4	uses `web3_item` and is delivered to the player's Backpack. Do not offer
5	`inventory_item`, Store API grants, direct Backpack grants, ERC-20 claim
6	endpoints or a provider-default catalog as fallbacks.
7	
8	These are the `parameters` of a node with `type: action` and
9	`subtype: issue_reward`:
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	  "type": "web3_item",
14	  "purpose": "quest_completion",
15	  "body": {
16	    "project": "<catalog project returned with the item>",
17	    "item_sku": "<catalog SKU>",
18	    "quantity": 1
19	  }
20	}
21	```
22	
23	The wrapper needs a supported `type`, a non-empty `purpose` and a non-empty
24	`body`. Use `quest_completion` for a named item unless the developer requests a
25	different reason.
26	
27	## Named item behavior
28	
29	When the publisher requests a named item (`<requested item>`):
30	
31	- resolve it only through an available supported reward capability (catalog or
32	  type-specific provider read). For production `web3_item`, the supported
33	  capability is the read-only minting catalog lookup documented in
34	  [auth and environment](auth-and-environment.md#minting-service). Page through
35	  the catalog, match the requested name, and validate candidate metadata before
36	  using it. Never use public web search for catalog lookup. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:**
37	  when the [stage demo gate](stage-demo.md#gate) passes, use the stage resolver
38	  described there; otherwise use production only;
39	- when the capability is available and returns exactly one verified candidate,
40	  use that candidate's catalog project and SKU in the `web3_item` body;
41	- when it returns multiple plausible candidates, ask the publisher to choose
42	  before any Quest Platform write;
43	- if the service is unavailable or rejects the read, stop before any Quest
44	  Platform write and report that the item lookup service could not be reached;
45	  do not say the publisher's catalog needs connecting. If a completed search
46	  returns zero candidates, say the item was not found and suggest checking its
47	  exact name or whether it is enabled. Do not ask the publisher to type a
48	  catalog project or SKU: a typed value is not a verified candidate;
49	- default quantity to one and show it in the concise proposal;
50	- never guess an SKU or silently substitute another reward type
51	  (`inventory_item`, Store API grants, direct Backpack grants, ERC-20 claim
52	  endpoints, or a provider-default catalog).
53	
54	Never ask whether the destination is Backpack. Preserve the catalog project
55	returned by the verified candidate; never copy the Quest Platform project as
56	the catalog project by default.
57	
58	## `web3_item`
59	
60	An NFT from the production minting catalog:
61	
62	```json
63	{
64	  "type": "web3_item",
65	  "purpose": "quest_completion",
66	  "body": {
67	    "project": "<catalog project>",
68	    "item_sku": "<string or array>",
69	    "quantity": 1
70	  }
71	}
72	```
73	
74	`quantity` must be a non-negative integer. For a named item, use a real SKU
75	returned by the catalog lookup. Omitting `item_sku` lets the provider choose an
76	item and is not allowed for a named reward.
77	
78	The production runtime must enforce the once-per-user-per-quest rule. When a
79	confirmed payout already exists for the same user and quest, a repeat event
80	must not mint a second item. If the earlier payout is unresolved, stop and
81	escalate rather than resend the event.
82	
83	## `web3_token`
84	
85	Production runs have ERC-20 payouts disabled: the production quest worker has
86	no ERC-20 project configured (`qp-worker-generic-quest/environments/prod/configs/configs.yaml`,
87	`WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT: ''`). A production quest with a `web3_token` action fails at
88	payout. When a production request asks for a token payout, stop before any
89	Quest Platform write, say that token payouts are not available for the project
90	yet, and offer a named item reward instead. Do not ask the publisher for a token
91	binding or decimals, because no production binding can make the payout work.
92	Use the shape below only when the selected target has ERC-20 enabled (the
93	`stage` selector today).
94	
95	An ERC-20 payout, only when the token binding and runtime contract for the
96	selected target are confirmed:
97	
98	```json
99	{
100	  "type": "web3_token",
101	  "purpose": "quest_completion",
102	  "body": {
103	    "project": "<token project>",
104	    "item_sku": "<bound token SKU>",
105	    "amount": 10000
106	  }
107	}
108	```
109	
110	`amount` must be a positive integer in the token's base units and within the
111	selected target's contract limit. Confirm the token decimals and binding with
112	the owner of that target. Never guess them.
113	
114	## Recipient
115

# Web3 rewards

This skill supports the production Web3 reward path only. A named item always
uses `web3_item` and is delivered to the player's Backpack. Do not offer
`inventory_item`, Store API grants, direct Backpack grants, ERC-20 claim
endpoints or a provider-default catalog as fallbacks.

These are the `parameters` of a node with `type: action` and
`subtype: issue_reward`:

```json
{
  "type": "web3_item",
  "purpose": "quest_completion",
  "body": {
    "project": "<catalog project returned with the item>",
    "item_sku": "<catalog SKU>",
    "quantity": 1
  }
}
```

The wrapper needs a supported `type`, a non-empty `purpose` and a non-empty
`body`. Use `quest_completion` for a named item unless the developer requests a
different reason.

## Named item behavior

When the publisher requests a named item (`<requested item>`):

- resolve it only through an available supported reward capability (catalog or
  type-specific provider read). For production `web3_item`, the supported
  capability is the read-only minting catalog lookup documented in
  [auth and environment](auth-and-environment.md#minting-service). Page through
  the catalog, match the requested name, and validate candidate metadata before
  using it. Never use public web search for catalog lookup. **STAGE DEMO ONLY:**
  when the [stage demo gate](stage-demo.md#gate) passes, use the stage resolver
  described there; otherwise use production only;
- when the capability is available and returns exactly one verified candidate,
  use that candidate's catalog project and SKU in the `web3_item` body;
- when it returns multiple plausible candidates, ask the publisher to choose
  before any Quest Platform write;
- if the service is unavailable or rejects the read, stop before any Quest
  Platform write and report that the item lookup service could not be reached;
  do not say the publisher's catalog needs connecting. If a completed search
  returns zero candidates, say the item was not found and suggest checking its
  exact name or whether it is enabled. Do not ask the publisher to type a
  catalog project or SKU: a typed value is not a verified candidate;
- default quantity to one and show it in the concise proposal;
- never guess an SKU or silently substitute another reward type
  (`inventory_item`, Store API grants, direct Backpack grants, ERC-20 claim
  endpoints, or a provider-default catalog).

Never ask whether the destination is Backpack. Preserve the catalog project
returned by the verified candidate; never copy the Quest Platform project as
the catalog project by default.

## `web3_item`

An NFT from the production minting catalog:

```json
{
  "type": "web3_item",
  "purpose": "quest_completion",
  "body": {
    "project": "<catalog project>",
    "item_sku": "<string or array>",
    "quantity": 1
  }
}
```

`quantity` must be a non-negative integer. For a named item, use a real SKU
returned by the catalog lookup. Omitting `item_sku` lets the provider choose an
item and is not allowed for a named reward.

The production runtime must enforce the once-per-user-per-quest rule. When a
confirmed payout already exists for the same user and quest, a repeat event
must not mint a second item. If the earlier payout is unresolved, stop and
escalate rather than resend the event.

## `web3_token`

Production runs have ERC-20 payouts disabled: the production quest worker has
no ERC-20 project configured (`qp-worker-generic-quest/environments/prod/configs/configs.yaml`,
`WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT: ''`). A production quest with a `web3_token` action fails at
payout. When a production request asks for a token payout, stop before any
Quest Platform write, say that token payouts are not available for the project
yet, and offer a named item reward instead. Do not ask the publisher for a token
binding or decimals, because no production binding can make the payout work.
Use the shape below only when the selected target has ERC-20 enabled (the
`stage` selector today).

An ERC-20 payout, only when the token binding and runtime contract for the
selected target are confirmed:

```json
{
  "type": "web3_token",
  "purpose": "quest_completion",
  "body": {
    "project": "<token project>",
    "item_sku": "<bound token SKU>",
    "amount": 10000
  }
}
```

`amount` must be a positive integer in the token's base units and within the
selected target's contract limit. Confirm the token decimals and binding with
the owner of that target. Never guess them.

## Recipient

Both Web3 reward types need an `xsolla_id` in the event and a production wallet
for that user. When a recipient is known, check the wallet during the
read-only work before the proposal, or otherwise before any publication write.
Check it again before the event. A missing wallet is a non-retryable blocker,
not an approval step. Confirm the wallet source is the Backpack-compatible
managed wallet required by the production integration.

## Payout exposure in the proposal

Show three bounds in the publication proposal:

- **Per event and user:** `web3_item` is `quantity × selected SKU count`;
  for a once-per-user named item at quantity one this is one NFT.
  `web3_token` is `amount`.
- **Per user for the quest:** apply the effective activation limit to the
  per-event quantity. For a confirmed once-per-user named item this is one NFT
  per user and quest; for quantity greater than one or multiple SKUs, multiply
  by `quantity × selected SKU count`. For `web3_token`, multiply `amount` by
  the maximum qualifying events for that user.
- **Total quest exposure:** multiply the per-user bound by the maximum number
  of eligible users. If the user population, event count, activation limit or
  date window is not finite, report the total as **unbounded**.

Do not publish a repeatable Web3 reward without showing these calculations in
the proposal. An unbounded total needs an explicit acknowledgement in that
same approval.

## Completion evidence

An execution marked `COMPLETED` proves only that the reward action completed
according to the production execution contract. It does not by itself prove a
Backpack display, wallet balance or on-chain finality. Report only the evidence
returned by the production read-back and never resend an event after an
uncertain result.

Attaching either reward type to an activated quest can create a real payout.
Show the reward and its exposure in the publication proposal; the one approval
covers activation of that exact configuration.

off=0
while :; do
  curl -sS --max-time 20 -o /tmp/p.json -w "offset $off HTTP %{http_code}\n" "$B/skus?project=316665&limit=100&offset=$off" || { echo "curl failed"; break; }
  python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
try:
    d=json.load(open("/tmp/p.json"))
    print("projectId",d.get("projectId"),"count",d.get("count"),"items",len(d.get("items",[])))
    for i in d.get("items",[]): print(json.dumps(i)[:200])
except Exception as e: print("bad body",open("/tmp/p.json").read()[:200])
EOF
  n=$(python3 -c 'import json;print(len(json.load(open("/tmp/p.json")).get("items",[])))' 2>/dev/null)
  [ "${n:-0}" -lt 1 ] && break
  off=$((off+100))
done; rm -f /tmp/p.json

1	# The quest document
2	
3	Use the versioned [Quest Platform publisher API contract](qp-api-contract.md)
4	for production route discovery. Production OpenAPI is intentionally
5	unavailable. Before writes, make a read-only request against the selected
6	public gateway; this reference does not replace checking the live response.
7	
8	Every quest route in this file is project-scoped. Below, `{scope}` stands for
9	the selected production project scope. The route family, credential and scope
10	rules are owned by the [versioned API contract](qp-api-contract.md). A 404
11	`text/plain` body `Cannot GET ...` means a wrong or old route, not a quest or
12	auth answer; follow [When a route is missing](auth-and-environment.md#when-a-route-is-missing).
13	
14	A quest is a **graph**, not a flat record. This one fact drives everything else
15	in this skill.
16	
17	## Fields
18	
19	`POST` and `PUT` take the whole quest object.
20	
21	| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| `name` | string | yes | 1 to 255 characters |
24	| `type` | string | yes | `liveops`, `ads`, `xsolla_app`, `social_quest`; see below. Use `liveops` internally for a gameplay quest unless the developer indicates another context; call it a gameplay quest in the publisher-facing preview |
25	| `status` | string | yes | `active` or `inactive` on write. `deleted` is set only by `DELETE`, a soft delete, and is rejected on write |
26	| `created_by` | string | yes | 1 to 255 characters. Use the developer's supplied name when available; otherwise use the internal label `AI Toolkit` without asking |
27	| `description` | string | no | if present, 5 to 1000 characters. Validate the live contract before relying on a server error message |
28	| `publisher_id` | string | server-set | set by the server from the selected production route. Never ask for it or invent it; on a `PUT`, send it back as the last read returned it |
29	| `project_id` | string | server-set | set by the server from the selected production route. On a `PUT`, send it exactly as the last read returned it. See Scope in the auth reference |
30	| `start_date` | RFC3339 | **only when `active`** | not earlier than exactly 24 hours before the server's now; see below |
31	| `end_date` | RFC3339 | **only when `active`** | not in the past, and at or after `start_date`. For a new quest without a requested end or duration, default to 7 days after the selected start; show this in the draft without asking for a date |
32	| `nodes` | array | **at least 2 when `active`** | optional and may be empty when `inactive` |
33	| `connections` | object | required unless `inactive` and empty | see below |
34	| `activation_limits` | array | no | see below |
35	| `metadata` | object | no | nesting depth at most 2 |
36	| `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `version_id` | mixed | server-assigned | ignored on create |
37	| `has_personalization` | bool | server-derived | `true` when any action is `webshop_personalization`, even though that action is a no-op at run time. Do not set it |
38	| `sample_data` | any | no | accepted, not validated, **not persisted** |
39	
40	The conditional requirements are enforced only by the server's hand-written
41	validator. They do not appear in the OpenAPI document.
42	
43	`type` is an API classification. The live contract must confirm the accepted
44	values and any downstream meaning. Keep it out of the normal publisher-facing
45	preview and use plain language such as "gameplay quest" instead. A loose match
46	such as "for the Xsolla app" is only a suggestion: ask a confirming question
47	before it goes into a body.
48	
49	The `start_date` check compares instants. When you refuse a start before
50	sending, explain the live rule in your own words, say nothing was sent, and
51	offer the earliest allowed start. To start now, take the current instant at
52	send time, not one computed earlier in the conversation.
53	
54	The `start_date` check runs on **every** write with `status: active`, including a `PUT`
55	that changes nothing else. A quest whose `start_date` is more than 24 hours old
56	cannot be saved as active without moving `start_date` forward. For such an edit,
57	show a proposed start at edit activation time in the before/after diff; if the
58	old `end_date` has passed, propose an end 7 days later. Ask for approval of the
59	revised edit, not a date. Both dates must be valid when the `PUT` is sent.
60	
61	A quest runs only while `active` and `start_date <= now <= end_date` at event
62	time. A future `start_date` is accepted, but events before it do not run the
63	quest; warn before sending an event outside the window.
64	
65	Dates are RFC3339 instants. State exact times in UTC whenever you show them,
66	including a fixed schedule in the draft and a publication read-back. Dates come back in the
67	server's local offset, for example `+03:00`, even when sent in `Z`; convert
68	them to UTC and compare instants, not strings.
69	
70	## Responses
71	
72	Create and update return 200, not 201, with the whole quest. Empty `nodes`,
73	`connections` and `metadata` come back as `null` rather than `[]` or `{}`;
74	that is not an error. An empty or absent optional field such as
75	`activation_limits` or `description` may come back as `null` or be omitted
76	from the response entirely; treat either as
77	not set. A `null` `nodes` may be sent back on an `inactive` quest; send real
78	arrays when activating. An optional field missing from a response is not set;
79	it is not `0` or an empty string. The list, `GET {scope}/quests`, returns
80	`{page, limit, total, data[]}`. Query: `page` (default 1; `0` is read as 1),
81	`limit` (default 10; `0` is read as 10; above 100 it is silently cut to 100,
82	with no error), `publisherID`. A non-integer value is 422. There is no name
83	filter: to find a quest by name, page through the whole list (a read-only name check before a create is optional, see Choosing a trigger in `node-subtypes.md`). Page through it
84	rather than reading one page as the whole list. Its items carry
85	`project_id` but no `publisher_id`, nodes, connections, dates or `account_id`,
86	so use the list only to find a quest's `id`; for anything else (the
87	`publisher` block, the graph, an edit) `GET {scope}/quests/{id}`. The list
88	covers only the route's project.
89	
90	`GET {scope}` (the project itself) returns `project_id` (integer), `name`,
91	`status`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and, only when set, `description`. It
92	carries no merchant, account or workspace id, so do not read one from it.
93	
94	## Publication after approval
95	
96	Before asking for approval of the draft quest, resolve the project, reward,
97	player action, complete graph, proposed schedule, and repeat limits. Use a
98	publisher-supplied start or propose activation time. Use a publisher-supplied
99	end, or add the supplied duration to the selected start, or default to 7 days.
100	Do not ask separately for dates or event-name approval. Inactive quests are an
101	internal write step only; they are not a separate user-facing draft workflow and are
102	excluded from the active public quest list.
103	
104	One approval of the exact publisher proposal authorizes this ordered sequence:
105	
106	1. `POST` a complete inactive quest with the full graph and reward from the
107	   approved proposal (required fields plus nodes and connections).
108	2. `GET` the created quest by id and confirm scope, graph, and reward.
109	3. Activate with the Editing recipe below (fresh `GET`, full `PUT`): set
110	   `status` to `active`, apply the approved `start_date`, `end_date`, and
111	   `activation_limits`. Everything else goes back verbatim. Do not ask a second
112	   approval for this activation `PUT`.
113	4. `GET` again and report active status, scope, reward, dates, limits, and
114	   `version_id`. Do not claim publication complete until this read-back matches
115	   the approved proposal.
116	
117	For "no repeat limit", sending `activation_limits` as `null` and leaving it out
118	are equivalent when the live contract treats the field as optional. `[]` may
119	also mean no limit; follow the live contract if these forms differ (see
120	Activation limits).
121	
122	A relative duration ("run it for 7 days") counts from the `start_date`
123	actually sent: `end_date` is that start plus 7x24 hours. If the start moves
124	(for example a requested time has passed), recompute the end under the approved
125	duration. Show a revised draft for approval only when this changes a fixed
126	schedule that the publisher explicitly requested.
127	
128	"Start now" is stamped when the activation `PUT` is built. Show the rule
129	("start at activation in UTC, end N days later") in the draft. The one approval
130	covers both timestamps, even when activation happens later than the draft was
131	shown. Report the actual UTC timestamps from the publication read-back.
132	
133	## Ambiguous or partial writes
134	
135	A `POST` that returned 200 created exactly one quest. Take the quest `id` from
136	that response. If it was not captured, find the quest by name in the list as
137	below; never send a second `POST` for the same proposal.
138	
139	After a timeout or 5xx on a quest `POST` or `PUT`, the write may have landed.
140	Reconcile with bounded read-back from the route contract before any retry:
141	
142	- For a `PUT`, `GET` the quest by id and compare to the intended document.
143	- For a `POST`, page the project list (`limit=100` from `page=1` until
144	  `page*limit >= total`) for the quest's `name`. Continue or repair the same
145	  quest when safe; never create a duplicate on timeout.
146	- Show what you found. Ask before any resend that would create a second quest.
147	- A 422 saved nothing: validation runs before anything is stored.
148	
149	Tell the publisher that publication did not finish, whether the quest is
150	visible, and the concrete next step. Never report publication complete until
151	the active quest and approved configuration read back.
152	
153	## Nodes and connections
154	
155	```json
156	{
157	  "nodes": [
158	    {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "<3-255 chars>", "type": "trigger", "subtype": "dynamic_event", "parameters": {}},
159	    {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "<3-255 chars>", "type": "action",  "subtype": "issue_reward",  "parameters": {}}
160	  ],
161	  "connections": {
162	    "<source node uuid>": [{"nodeId": "<target node uuid>", "on": "ticket_issued"}]
163	  }
164	}
165	```
166	
167	- `type` is `trigger`, `action` or `condition`.
168	- `id` must be a valid, non-zero UUID.
169	- `on` is optional. An edge without it is always followed. With it, the
170	  runtime follows the edge only when the source action returns that outcome:
171	  `ticket_issued`, `no_ticket` or `daily_cap_reached`. Only an `issue_reward`
172	  with `vc_wallet_ticket` `playtime` returns these outcomes today.
173	- Every edge must reference a node that exists in `nodes`, and the graph must
174	  be acyclic.
175	
176	The smallest quest that can be activated is two nodes and one edge: a trigger
177	and an action.
178	
179	Name nodes after what they do, and label anything that is not real in the
180	name, for example `noop` or `webhook (placeholder)`, so a later read shows it.
181	
182	### Several actions on one trigger
183	
184	The quest runtime walks the graph depth-first from the trigger, one node at a time,
185	in the order the edges are listed under each source node. Several actions on
186	one trigger therefore run one after another, not in parallel. They are not
187	independent:
188	
189	- The first node that fails stops the whole walk. Nodes after it, including
190	  sibling actions listed later, do not run.
191	- One failed action makes the whole execution `FAILED`
192	  (`failReason: ACTION_FAILED`). Actions that already succeeded are not
193	  rolled back: a reward or notification sent before the failure stays sent.
194	  A later failure does not roll back an earlier external action.
195	- A condition miss also stops the walk; see `conditions.md`.
196	- On the next event for the same user and quest, the runtime skips nodes that
197	  already succeeded in the failed run and retries the rest according to the
198	  production runtime contract.
199	
200	How the edges are listed decides the shape. For "A then B" on trigger `T`,
201	either form runs A before B, but they differ when A has an `on` outcome:
202	
203	```json
204	{"T": [{"nodeId": "A"}, {"nodeId": "B"}]}
205	```
206	
207	Siblings: both hang off the trigger, in list order. B runs after A whatever
208	outcome A returned (unless A failed).
209	
210	```json
211	{"T": [{"nodeId": "A"}], "A": [{"nodeId": "B"}]}
212	```
213	
214	Chain: B hangs off A, so an `on` on the `A -> B` edge can gate B on A's
215	outcome. Without `on`, both shapes run the same way. The keys and `nodeId`s
216	are node UUIDs; the letters here are placeholders.
217	
218	So put the action whose failure should block the others first, and tell the
219	developer that a later failure does not undo an earlier payout. How to read
220	per-action statuses is in [`verification.md`](verification.md).
221	
222	## Activation limits
223	
224	```json
225	{"activation_limits": [{"type": "per_user", "count": 1, "time_window": {"duration_unit": "day"}}]}
226	```
227	
228	`type` is `global` or `per_user`. `count` must be at least 1.
229	`time_window.duration_unit`, when present, is `day`, `week` or `month`.
230	If `activation_limits` is absent, `null` or empty, no repeat limit is
231	configured: every qualifying event runs the actions. Show that unlimited-repeat
232	behavior, and the resulting payout impact, inside the publication proposal so
233	the one approval covers it. Do not ask again for the activation `PUT` unless a
234	material value changed after approval, in which case show the revised proposal
235	and request approval again. Never silently assume a one-time or per-user limit.
236	
237	A limit without `time_window` counts over the quest's whole life: `per_user`
238	`count: 1` means once per user, ever. A retest then needs a new user or a new
239	quest. With `time_window`, the count resets each calendar day, week or month.
240	A Web3 reward has its own repeat rule on top; see `rewards.md`.
241	
242	During the read-only work before the proposal, and before the first write,
243	check that the intended trigger reaches an intended action and that no intended
244	node is orphaned. The server validates references and cycles, but those checks
245	alone do not prove that the quest is semantically usable.
246	
247	## Editing
248	
249	There is **no PATCH**. Update is a full-document `PUT`: read the quest, change
250	what you need, and send the whole object back. Tell the developer this before
251	editing, because a partial body silently drops everything it omits.
252	
253	Recipe: take the body of a fresh `GET`, change only the fields the developer
254	asked for, and send the rest verbatim, `null` values included. Keep the
255	server-assigned fields (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `version_id`,
256	`has_personalization`) as read: the server ignores them on `PUT` (the path
257	`id` wins). `has_personalization` turns `true` in the next read after a
258	`webshop_personalization` (no-op) node is added; that is expected, not a diff
259	to report as a change. A `$schema` link may be present; drop it before the
260	`PUT`. For a new node, you generate its `id` as a fresh random UUID (v4); the
261	server does not assign node ids, and existing node ids stay unchanged. Show the
262	before/after diff of the changed fields before sending.
263	
264	An edit to an active quest applies to the next events after the production
265	configuration propagation window. Repeat the activation confirmations
266	for the changed part when the edit touches any of: an action's subtype or
267	parameters, connections that change which actions run, a reward, the
268	activation limits, the dates, or `status`. An edit to `name` or
269	`description` only needs no repeat. If the edit changes an amount or SKU,
270	check node names that mention the old value. Whenever a reward changes, also
271	check whether the quest name still describes it. If the name mentions the old
272	reward (for example, Fire Sword changed to Ice Sword), update the quest name in
273	the same proposed edit and include it in the before/after diff. Ask only if the
274	intended new name is unclear. The reward-change confirmation covers the
275	combined reward and name edit.
276	
277	`version_id` is server-assigned and changes on every write. It is ignored in
278	the body: there is no optimistic concurrency, quest `PUT` never returns 409,
279	and the last write wins. Read the quest immediately before a `PUT`.
280	
281	## Pausing
282	
283	There is no pause route. To pause, send the full-document `PUT` from the recipe
284	with `status: inactive` and keep the dates, nodes and limits as they are. The
285	date rules apply only to `active` writes, so an old `start_date` is fine here;
286	reactivating later runs them again (see Fields).
287	
288	While the quest is inactive, events do not run the inactive configuration and
289	are not replayed automatically on reactivation. During the production
290	propagation window, an event may still see the previous configuration; warn
291	before sending an event for a quest with an external reward.

cannot be saved as active without moving `start_date` forward. For such an edit,
show a proposed start at edit activation time in the before/after diff; if the
old `end_date` has passed, propose an end 7 days later. Ask for approval of the
revised edit, not a date. Both dates must be valid when the `PUT` is sent.

A quest runs only while `active` and `start_date <= now <= end_date` at event
time. A future `start_date` is accepted, but events before it do not run the
quest; warn before sending an event outside the window.

Dates are RFC3339 instants. State exact times in UTC whenever you show them,
including a fixed schedule in the draft and a publication read-back. Dates come back in the
server's local offset, for example `+03:00`, even when sent in `Z`; convert
them to UTC and compare instants, not strings.

## Responses

Create and update return 200, not 201, with the whole quest. Empty `nodes`,
`connections` and `metadata` come back as `null` rather than `[]` or `{}`;
that is not an error. An empty or absent optional field such as
`activation_limits` or `description` may come back as `null` or be omitted
from the response entirely; treat either as
not set. A `null` `nodes` may be sent back on an `inactive` quest; send real
arrays when activating. An optional field missing from a response is not set;
it is not `0` or an empty string. The list, `GET {scope}/quests`, returns
`{page, limit, total, data[]}`. Query: `page` (default 1; `0` is read as 1),
`limit` (default 10; `0` is read as 10; above 100 it is silently cut to 100,
with no error), `publisherID`. A non-integer value is 422. There is no name
filter: to find a quest by name, page through the whole list (a read-only name check before a create is optional, see Choosing a trigger in `node-subtypes.md`). Page through it
rather than reading one page as the whole list. Its items carry
`project_id` but no `publisher_id`, nodes, connections, dates or `account_id`,
so use the list only to find a quest's `id`; for anything else (the
`publisher` block, the graph, an edit) `GET {scope}/quests/{id}`. The list
covers only the route's project.

`GET {scope}` (the project itself) returns `project_id` (integer), `name`,
`status`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and, only when set, `description`. It
carries no merchant, account or workspace id, so do not read one from it.

## Publication after approval

Before asking for approval of the draft quest, resolve the project, reward,
player action, complete graph, proposed schedule, and repeat limits. Use a
publisher-supplied start or propose activation time. Use a publisher-supplied
end, or add the supplied duration to the selected start, or default to 7 days.
Do not ask separately for dates or event-name approval. Inactive quests are an
internal write step only; they are not a separate user-facing draft workflow and are
excluded from the active public quest list.

One approval of the exact publisher proposal authorizes this ordered sequence:

1. `POST` a complete inactive quest with the full graph and reward from the
   approved proposal (required fields plus nodes and connections).
2. `GET` the created quest by id and confirm scope, graph, and reward.
3. Activate with the Editing recipe below (fresh `GET`, full `PUT`): set
   `status` to `active`, apply the approved `start_date`, `end_date`, and
   `activation_limits`. Everything else goes back verbatim. Do not ask a second
   approval for this activation `PUT`.
4. `GET` again and report active status, scope, reward, dates, limits, and
   `version_id`. Do not claim publication complete until this read-back matches
   the approved proposal.

For "no repeat limit", sending `activation_limits` as `null` and leaving it out
are equivalent when the live contract treats the field as optional. `[]` may
also mean no limit; follow the live contract if these forms differ (see
Activation limits).

A relative duration ("run it for 7 days") counts from the `start_date`
actually sent: `end_date` is that start plus 7x24 hours. If the start moves
(for example a requested time has passed), recompute the end under the approved
duration. Show a revised draft for approval only when this changes a fixed
schedule that the publisher explicitly requested.

"Start now" is stamped when the activation `PUT` is built. Show the rule
("start at activation in UTC, end N days later") in the draft. The one approval
covers both timestamps, even when activation happens later than the draft was
shown. Report the actual UTC timestamps from the publication read-back.

## Ambiguous or partial writes

A `POST` that returned 200 created exactly one quest. Take the quest `id` from
that response. If it was not captured, find the quest by name in the list as
below; never send a second `POST` for the same proposal.

After a timeout or 5xx on a quest `POST` or `PUT`, the write may have landed.
Reconcile with bounded read-back from the route contract before any retry:

- For a `PUT`, `GET` the quest by id and compare to the intended document.
- For a `POST`, page the project list (`limit=100` from `page=1` until
  `page*limit >= total`) for the quest's `name`. Continue or repair the same
  quest when safe; never create a duplicate on timeout.
- Show what you found. Ask before any resend that would create a second quest.
- A 422 saved nothing: validation runs before anything is stored.

Tell the publisher that publication did not finish, whether the quest is
visible, and the concrete next step. Never report publication complete until
the active quest and approved configuration read back.

## Nodes and connections

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "<3-255 chars>", "type": "trigger", "subtype": "dynamic_event", "parameters": {}},
    {"id": "<uuid>", "name": "<3-255 chars>", "type": "action",  "subtype": "issue_reward",  "parameters": {}}
  ],
  "connections": {
    "<source node uuid>": [{"nodeId": "<target node uuid>", "on": "ticket_issued"}]
  }
}
```

- `type` is `trigger`, `action` or `condition`.
- `id` must be a valid, non-zero UUID.
- `on` is optional. An edge without it is always followed. With it, the
  runtime follows the edge only when the source action returns that outcome:
  `ticket_issued`, `no_ticket` or `daily_cap_reached`. Only an `issue_reward`
  with `vc_wallet_ticket` `playtime` returns these outcomes today.
- Every edge must reference a node that exists in `nodes`, and the graph must
  be acyclic.

The smallest quest that can be activated is two nodes and one edge: a trigger
and an action.

Name nodes after what they do, and label anything that is not real in the
name, for example `noop` or `webhook (placeholder)`, so a later read shows it.

### Several actions on one trigger

The quest runtime walks the graph depth-first from the trigger, one node at a time,
in the order the edges are listed under each source node. Several actions on
one trigger therefore run one after another, not in parallel. They are not
independent:

- The first node that fails stops the whole walk. Nodes after it, including
  sibling actions listed later, do not run.
- One failed action makes the whole execution `FAILED`
  (`failReason: ACTION_FAILED`). Actions that already succeeded are not
  rolled back: a reward or notification sent before the failure stays sent.
  A later failure does not roll back an earlier external action.
- A condition miss also stops the walk; see `conditions.md`.
- On the next event for the same user and quest, the runtime skips nodes that
  already succeeded in the failed run and retries the rest according to the
  production runtime contract.

How the edges are listed decides the shape. For "A then B" on trigger `T`,
either form runs A before B, but they differ when A has an `on` outcome:

```json
{"T": [{"nodeId": "A"}, {"nodeId": "B"}]}
```

Siblings: both hang off the trigger, in list order. B runs after A whatever
outcome A returned (unless A failed).

```json
{"T": [{"nodeId": "A"}], "A": [{"nodeId": "B"}]}
```

Chain: B hangs off A, so an `on` on the `A -> B` edge can gate B on A's
outcome. Without `on`, both shapes run the same way. The keys and `nodeId`s
are node UUIDs; the letters here are placeholders.

So put the action whose failure should block the others first, and tell the
developer that a later failure does not undo an earlier payout. How to read
per-action statuses is in [`verification.md`](verification.md).

## Activation limits

```json
{"activation_limits": [{"type": "per_user", "count": 1, "time_window": {"duration_unit": "day"}}]}
```

`type` is `global` or `per_user`. `count` must be at least 1.
`time_window.duration_unit`, when present, is `day`, `week` or `month`.
If `activation_limits` is absent, `null` or empty, no repeat limit is
configured: every qualifying event runs the actions. Show that unlimited-repeat
behavior, and the resulting payout impact, inside the publication proposal so
the one approval covers it. Do not ask again for the activation `PUT` unless a
material value changed after approval, in which case show the revised proposal
and request approval again. Never silently assume a one-time or per-user limit.

A limit without `time_window` counts over the quest's whole life: `per_user`
`count: 1` means once per user, ever. A retest then needs a new user or a new
quest. With `time_window`, the count resets each calendar day, week or month.
A Web3 reward has its own repeat rule on top; see `rewards.md`.

During the read-only work before the proposal, and before the first write,
check that the intended trigger reaches an intended action and that no intended
node is orphaned. The server validates references and cycles, but those checks
alone do not prove that the quest is semantically usable.

## Editing

There is **no PATCH**. Update is a full-document `PUT`: read the quest, change
what you need, and send the whole object back. Tell the developer this before
editing, because a partial body silently drops everything it omits.

Recipe: take the body of a fresh `GET`, change only the fields the developer
asked for, and send the rest verbatim, `null` values included. Keep the
server-assigned fields (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `version_id`,
`has_personalization`) as read: the server ignores them on `PUT` (the path
`id` wins). `has_personalization` turns `true` in the next read after a
`webshop_personalization` (no-op) node is added; that is expected, not a diff
to report as a change. A `$schema` link may be present; drop it before the
`PUT`. For a new node, you generate its `id` as a fresh random UUID (v4); the
server does not assign node ids, and existing node ids stay unchanged. Show the
before/after diff of the changed fields before sending.

An edit to an active quest applies to the next events after the production
configuration propagation window. Repeat the activation confirmations
for the changed part when the edit touches any of: an action's subtype or
parameters, connections that change which actions run, a reward, the
activation limits, the dates, or `status`. An edit to `name` or
`description` only needs no repeat. If the edit changes an amount or SKU,
check node names that mention the old value. Whenever a reward changes, also
check whether the quest name still describes it. If the name mentions the old
reward (for example, Fire Sword changed to Ice Sword), update the quest name in
the same proposed edit and include it in the before/after diff. Ask only if the
intended new name is unclear. The reward-change confirmation covers the
combined reward and name edit.

`version_id` is server-assigned and changes on every write. It is ignored in
the body: there is no optimistic concurrency, quest `PUT` never returns 409,
and the last write wins. Read the quest immediately before a `PUT`.

## Pausing

There is no pause route. To pause, send the full-document `PUT` from the recipe
with `status: inactive` and keep the dates, nodes and limits as they are. The
date rules apply only to `active` writes, so an old `start_date` is fine here;
reactivating later runs them again (see Fields).

While the quest is inactive, events do not run the inactive configuration and
are not replayed automatically on reactivation. During the production
propagation window, an event may still see the previous configuration; warn
before sending an event for a quest with an external reward.

**Defeat a monster: Fire Sword**
- **Status:** active
- **Runs:** 2 Oct 2026 10:48:26 UTC to 9 Oct 2026 10:48:26 UTC
- **Trigger:** a player defeats a monster (`monster_defeated`)
- **Reward:** 1 Fire Sword (Web3 item)
- **Repeat limit:** once per player
- **Version:** `2f6c2dc8-5989-4862-912a-ad0b46f3111e`

This confirms the quest is configured. It doesn't show that any reward has been delivered.

## Next step: test event (optional)

I haven't sent an event. If you want to try the quest, I can send one for a player. A real Fire Sword will be issued to that player, and because of the once-per-player limit a repeat won't pay again. I need the player's Xsolla user ID, and the player needs a Backpack wallet.

The payload would look like this:

```json
{
  "idempotency_key": "<new UUID>",
  "name": "monster_defeated",
  "client_timestamp": "<current time, RFC3339>",
  "user_ids": [{"identifier_type": "xsolla_id", "value": "<player's Xsolla user ID>"}],
  "publisher": {"publisher_id": "940463", "project_id": "316665"}
}
```

Send me the user ID and I'll show you the final payload to approve before anything goes out.

Never a top-level nav tab, 5 router entry, or new shop route. 6 7 Triggers: "show quests in my web shop", "add quest module to shop", "quest 8 module", "catalog quests section". 9 10 ## When to use 11 12 - **New shop** (during or after shop-setup): ask / confirm opt-in before adding. 13 - **Existing shop**: when the developer asks to add or update quests in the 14 shop, run the upsert algorithm below. 15 16 An explicit request to integrate quests into an existing shop authorizes the 17 source edits. Do not respond with a plan that asks for approval, an open 18 question about language, or a request for the endpoint URL. Infer locale from 19 the shop's existing localization setup and use the configured public API 20 contract. Give a brief progress update only when the work takes long enough to 21 need one, then make the edits and run the shop's available checks. 22 23 Out of scope: user progress / completion UI, fabricating sample quests, 24 changing AdTech APIs, Site Builder blocks. 25 26 ## Identity (source of truth) 27 28 **Required marker** on the module root: 29 30 ```html 31
32 ``` 33 34 The attribute `data-xsolla-quest-module` is the only required identity. 35 An optional file hint `**/XsollaQuestModule.{tsx,jsx,ts,js}` may exist; prefer 36 updating the marked root when both are present. Images: use the reward name as `alt` when informative, 159 or empty `alt` when decorative. Never a top-level nav tab, router entry, or new shop route. Triggers: "show quests in my web shop", "add quest module to shop", "quest module", "catalog quests section". ## When to use - **New shop** (during or after shop-setup): ask / confirm opt-in before adding. - **Existing shop**: when the developer asks to add or update quests in the shop, run the upsert algorithm below. An explicit request to integrate quests into an existing shop authorizes the source edits. Do not respond with a plan that asks for approval, an open question about language, or a request for the endpoint URL. Infer locale from the shop's existing localization setup and use the configured public API contract. Give a brief progress update only when the work takes long enough to need one, then make the edits and run the shop's available checks. Out of scope: user progress / completion UI, fabricating sample quests, changing AdTech APIs, Site Builder blocks. ## Identity (source of truth) **Required marker** on the module root: ```html
``` The attribute `data-xsolla-quest-module` is the only required identity. An optional file hint `**/XsollaQuestModule.{tsx,jsx,ts,js}` may exist; prefer updating the marked root when both are present. Do not require React. **Stack adaptors (ordered):** 1. Detect the catalog page stack (React / Vue / Svelte / static HTML+JS / other). 2. Add or update a same-stack module that renders the marked root. 3. Default **new** shops to **static HTML + vanilla JS** unless the catalog page is already a component framework. ## Config and IDs Use the merchant/project pair resolved from the connected Quest Platform project. Do not assume the shop's Store catalog project ID is the Quest Platform project ID; they can differ. Reuse the shop's merchant ID only after confirming it matches the resolved Quest Platform merchant. Keep the Store catalog project setting intact, and give the Quest Platform project its own browser-safe setting when it differs. Never copy IDs from an example or infer one ID from the other. The public API host is selected automatically from the active Quest Platform environment: production by default, stage only when the developer explicitly selected a controlled stage run. The storefront URL is formed from that host and the resolved Quest Platform scope; do not ask the developer to find or provide a URL. For browser code, expose only the resolved IDs and public URL as build-time configuration. Prefer the shop's existing variable naming (`VITE_*` for Vite, `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` for Next.js). The full URL may be stored as an override only when the project already has a URL override setting or the developer supplied an exact URL. | Variable | Role | |---|---| | `XSOLLA_QP_MERCHANT_ID` | Path `merchant_id` | | `XSOLLA_QP_PROJECT_ID` | Path `project_id`; separate from the Store catalog project when they differ | | `XSOLLA_QP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | Optional explicit public-base override; production host is the default | For browser builds, use the shop's public-variable convention, for example `VITE_XSOLLA_QP_MERCHANT_ID` and `VITE_XSOLLA_QP_PROJECT_ID` in Vite, or `NEXT_PUBLIC_XSOLLA_QP_MERCHANT_ID` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_XSOLLA_QP_PROJECT_ID` in Next.js. Keep existing Store variables such as `VITE_XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` for catalog and checkout calls. Never expose the Quest Platform API key in browser configuration. `XSOLLA_QP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is **not** a substitute for the agent CRUD host table in [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md). Agents keep using that table for qp-server writes. The storefront uses the selected public host and resolved merchant/project IDs only for the public list. **Hard stops:** - Use `https://quests-platform.xsolla.com` when the environment selector is absent or `production`; use `https://quests-stage.xsolla.com` only for an explicitly selected controlled stage run. A configured public-base override takes precedence after validation. - Resolve the Quest Platform merchant/project pair from the connected Quest Platform scope. Compare it with the shop's existing merchant and Store project settings; use the Store project setting for quests only if it is confirmed to be the same Quest Platform project. If the Quest Platform scope cannot be resolved, ask which connected Quest Platform project to use; never ask the developer to find or provide the API URL. - Do **not** set the storefront public base to `https://qp-server.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` (or any `*.srv.local`) for a **publicly reachable** shop. That stage host is corporate/VPN-only. Stage browser proof needs VPN, or is agent-side smoke only. - Never put API keys or `Authorization` in browser code for this module. ## Wire contract (consume verbatim) `GET {base}/api/v2/public/merchants/{merchant_id}/projects/{project_id}/quests?page=1&limit=100` No auth header. The maximum page size is 100. Build `{base}` from the selected environment default or an existing validated override. **200 envelope:** `page`, `limit`, `total`, `data[]` with: | Field | Rule | |---|---| | `data[].id` | Required string (UUID); list key | | `data[].name` | Required string | | `data[].description` | Optional; omit when absent | | `data[].rewards` | Required array (may be empty) | | `rewards[].name`, `rewards[].description`, `rewards[].image_url` | Present; may be **null** — skip nulls when rendering | | `rewards[].quantity` | Required int | | `rewards[].type` | Required string | Empty success is a 200 response with `data: []`. Do not describe a failed request as an empty quest list. A JSON 404 means the merchant/project pair is unknown, not onboarded, or mismatched; re-check the resolved pair and active environment without guessing. Plain-text `Cannot GET ` means the route is unavailable at that host or the path is wrong. A 422, network, or CORS failure is also unavailable, not empty. Show the neutral unavailable message for fetch or missing-configuration errors, and keep the catalog working. Never fabricate quests or rewards. ## Markup shape ```html

Quests are configured by the publisher. Rewards are delivered to your Backpack.

Loading quests...

No active quests right now.

``` **Fixed copy (exact):** - Disclaimer: `Quests are configured by the publisher. Rewards are delivered to your Backpack.` - Empty: `No active quests right now.` - Neutral error (optional): `Quests are temporarily unavailable.` Place as a sibling **inside** the catalog content container (after or before the product list). `, header tabs, or a top-level tablist. **Accessibility:** empty and error text must stay visible (not `display:none`-only). Use responsive layout rules for narrow screens: allow titles and descriptions to wrap, keep reward media from collapsing, and avoid horizontal overflow. Do not add a new navigation tab, route, or unrelated visual treatment. Skip relative, `javascript:`, `data:`, and other schemes. CORS depends on the server `ALLOW_ORIGINS` setting. On CORS failure, show the neutral error (or hide the module) and keep the catalog working. When the shop is served over `https`, the public base must also be `https` (no mixed-content HTTP). Never send credentials (`credentials: 'include'`) on this fetch. ## Idempotent upsert algorithm 1. Resolve the Quest Platform merchant/project pair from the connected scope. Compare it with shop settings, keeping the Store catalog project ID separate unless it is confirmed to be the same project. Use dedicated browser-safe Quest Platform settings when needed. If either ID is unresolved, stop and ask which connected Quest Platform project to use; never substitute sample IDs or silently reuse the catalog ID. Select the public base automatically (production by default; stage only for an explicit controlled stage run). Do not ask for a URL. 2. Confirm opt-in for new shops; for existing shops proceed when the developer asks to add/update the quest module. 3. **Preflight marker count** across the shop tree for `data-xsolla-quest-module`: - **0** → insert one marked section **inside** the catalog content container (never nav / router / top-level tab). Create the component file once if the stack uses files; mount it once. - **1** → update that root **in place**. Prefer patching fetch URL, IDs, null-skip logic, safe rendering, and the fixed disclaimer / empty / error strings. Preserve publisher CSS and customizations outside the managed region. Do not create a second file or second marked section. - **>1** → **stop and ask** before writing. Do not auto-dedupe. 4. If a `XsollaQuestModule` file exists without a marker, update the file so the root carries the marker, then ensure **exactly one** catalog mount. 5. Before writing, count imports and calls for the module in the bootstrap: if either count is greater than `1`, stop and ask. If one exists, update it in place with the current module path, resolved Quest Platform IDs, and base URL. Check the active local/build configuration for the required public IDs; do not mistake a sample or `.env.example` value for a configured value. If a required value is missing, use the resolved scope to configure the shop's local environment file with browser-safe IDs only, and restart the dev server so Vite or the equivalent reloads build-time variables. If the scope cannot be resolved, stop and ask instead of writing a placeholder. If none exists, add one import and one mount. Preserve unrelated bootstrap code. 6. content.text:
## Plan: add a quests section to the Voidwall shop

I've only read the shop so far. I haven't changed anything.

The shop is a Vite + React app. Its catalog page renders inside `<main className="page">` in `src/App.tsx`. There's no quest section yet, so there's nothing to merge or dedupe. Its Store project is the same Quest Platform project the Fire Sword quest is published in.

- **Component:** add `src/components/XsollaQuestModule.tsx`, rendering one marked `<section data-xsolla-quest-module="1" aria-label="Quests">`. It shows a card per quest with its reward row (name, quantity, type badge, image only if the URL is absolute http/https). It also has loading, empty and "Quests are temporarily unavailable." states.
- **Data:** it fetches the public quest list from the production public gateway with no auth header and no credentials. Quest and reward text goes through React text children only, with no `innerHTML`. If the fetch fails, the catalog keeps working.
- **Placement:** mount it once in `src/App.tsx` inside the catalog content, next to the existing sections. It does not go in the header, nav or a new route.
- **Config:** add `VITE_XSOLLA_QP_MERCHANT_ID` and `VITE_XSOLLA_QP_PROJECT_ID` to `src/config.ts`, `.env` and `.env.example`. These are browser-safe IDs only, and the API key stays out of the browser. The existing `VITE_XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` is untouched.
- **Styling and checks:** I'll style it in `src/theme.css` to match the shop. I'll add a test in `tests/` for the render states and safe rendering, then run `npm test` and `npm run build`.

Reply **yes** to go ahead, or tell me what to change.
